gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false global-singleton claim: local implicit-function uniqueness is incorrectly used to treat the globally infimized cost as the selected branch cost.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The global solution set may contain branches outside the local uniqueness neighborhood, so the infimum-defined reduced functional is not justified as the smooth cost of the selected branch.

component_coverage.gold_component: Global singleton/branch identification fails, invalidating identification of the global infimum cost with the local smooth branch cost.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that uniqueness is only local, other solutions may exist, and the infimum may be attained on another branch, making the derivative formulas unsupported.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The prediction concerns nonuniqueness of state branches and the global reduced functional, whereas the gold defect is the missing desired-state L^p hypothesis required by the adjoint maximum-norm estimate.

The prediction recognizes that an arbitrary semidiscrete solution need not belong to the convergent local branch, but it does not diagnose the separate failure that J_h is never defined when the discrete state is nonunique.

Both identify that existence of an arbitrary semidiscrete solution does not provide convergence to the prescribed local solution; the proof and rate require the specifically constructed localized convergent sequence.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The convergence and error theorem is stated for an arbitrary solution even though only the selected sequence of localized local minimizers is known to converge to the prescribed control.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem confuses an arbitrary existent semidiscrete solution with the specifically constructed convergent local-minimizer sequence.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that the existence theorem gives only some solution, convergence is proved only for localized minimizers, and the proof improperly applies convergence-dependent estimates to the arbitrary solution named in the statement.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the invalid inference of an O(h^2) gradient error from an O(h^2) L^2 error using interpolation and inverse estimates, despite the continuous interpolation remainder being only O(h).
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed h^2 derivative/gradient approximation does not follow from the available H^2 regularity and L^2 state error; the inverse estimate applies only to the finite-element component, not the full continuous-discrete error.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof falsely derives an O(h^2) gradient error from an O(h^2) L^2 error, ignoring the lower-order interpolation remainder.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the interpolation-plus-inverse decomposition, obtains O(h) rather than O(h^2), and explains why the stated regularity and bang-bang control prevent the stronger rate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The corrected argument must avoid the false gradient estimate and use a different residual/adjoint estimate to establish the rate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction supplies the corresponding consequence and a specific alternative maximum-norm/stability repair or rate downgrade, demonstrating recognition of the failed estimate's role in the control-rate proof.
